characters.name: Rev. Geraldine Granger
characters.description: All Girls Want Bad Boys: Her reaction to Simon Horton's description of himself as the too much drinking and too much sex "prodigal" brother is to be visibly turned on... but she's turned very off when he dumps her for his ex. Alliterative Name:GeraldineGranger Big Beautiful Woman: The village certainly seems to think Geraldine is, with constant references to her "lovely arse." Big-Breast Pride: She's quite proud of her "magnificent bosom." Big Eater: Shelovesher chocolate. She also has a very large freezer dedicated solely to ice cream. When she's upset, she eatsmore than should behumanly possible.

characters.name: David Horton
characters.description: Abhorrent Admirer: To Geraldine in the third series. Bald of Evil: Well, pretty evil in the first episodes. Belligerent Sexual Tension: With Geraldine, though it's decidedly one-sided. David was so used to arguing with people that he misinterpreted Geraldine's resistance to him as genuine affection. She does care about him in a weird way,just not in that way. Birds of a Feather:Subverted. He does fall for Geraldine, but sheturns him down becausejustbeing the only two sane people in the village doesn't mean they should be married. British Stuffiness: His reaction when Hugo hugs him is to stand stock-still and look uncomfortable.

characters.name: Alice Tinker Horton
characters.description: Cloud Cuckoo Lander:So. Very. Much.For example, she thinks the Wombles were real and Geraldine's attempt to explain that they were people in costume goes nowhere. The Comically Serious: Alice's reaction to some of Geraldine's jokesat the end of each episode. Conspiracy Theorist:She reallycan'tbelieve "I Can't Believe It's Not Butter" (or its generic imitation, "I Can't Believe It's Not 'I Can't Believe It's Not Butter'") is not butter... and there may be a lot more butter around than anyone realizes.She thinks thatshe is the descendant of Jesus and Mary Magdalene. She reallycan'tbelieve "I Can't Believe It's Not Butter" (or its generic imitation, "I Can't Believe It's Not 'I Can't Believe It's Not Butter'") is not butter... and there may be a lot more butter around than anyone realizes. She thinks thatshe is the descendant of Jesus and Mary Magdalene.

characters.name: Hugo Horton
characters.description: Alliterative Name:HugoHorton Armor-Piercing Response: When his father puts to him a threat that marrying the woman David loathes most because he loves her will result in Hugo losing any inheritance from David and so have nothing, Hugo calmly tells his father in marrying the woman he loves he will have all that he desires. David is at a lose for any response and stops opposing the union. Birds of a Feather: With Alice. As Geraldine notes, Alice may have the wit and intelligence of a cactus, but Hugo is "cactus-man." Buffy Speak: "Yes, Father, everyone's fed up to the teeth with you shouting at them all the time! Like some big, bald, shouty-type person...." Calling the Old Man Out: First he calls out David for being childish and spitefully trying to get Geraldine sacked over the animal mass. Andthenthere's the episode where David tries to invoke theParental Marriage Veto...David:And as this will attests, you will havenothing! [thrusts paper at Hugo]Hugo:[looks at paper and hands it back] On the contrary, sir, I will have everything in the world that I desire.

characters.name: Owen Newitt
characters.description: Abhorrent Admirer: To Geraldine from the second season onward. All Men Are Perverts: He's probably the worse one between himself and Jim. After proposing to (and being rejected) by Geraldine, he continues to make lewd comments about her at the slightest provocation. Bestiality Is Depraved: He is open and shameless about his"relationships"with animals. We'll leave it at that. Big, Screwed-Up Family: Several of his relatives have committed suicide or murder, and his grandfather murdered his grandmother and hid her under the floorboards. Chivalrous Pervert: He's a crude serial flirt towards Geraldine, but he leaps to her defense against David when she dates Simon Horton, arguing that as long as she's discreet, she's got just as much right to a sex life as anyone else does, vicar or not. "Though I wouldn't mind a few Polaroids."

characters.name: Jim Trott
characters.description: Catchphrase: "No, no, no, no, no, no, no,yes." Citizenship Marriage: At one time in his life he got married on a beach in Southeast Asia and only learned on the honeymoon that it was a bloke called Dwayne after a passport. (They still "more than snogged" though.) Confusing Multiple Negatives: A man trying to park his car during the town fair comes up to him while he's doing P.A. announcements asking for clarification whether he is or is not supposed to park in the upper field, having mistaken "No, no, no, no, no parking on the upper field" for self-negating negatives. Regular viewers will know by now that thelastword of Jim'sVerbal Ticis the one he actually means: you don't count and multiply them. Dirty Old Man: He makes frequent references to his love of porn and sexual (mis)adventures. Heterosexual Life-Partners: With Frank. They make sure to remind Geraldine how platonic it is when they invite her to Christmas lunch.

characters.name: Frank Pickle
characters.description: Ambiguously Bi: Before coming out as gay (revealing that he has known he is gay since World War II), Frank is revealed to have fathered a child with Owen's cousin Sally, and confesses to a crush on politician Margaret Beckett. The Bore: Frank is this to a T. His idea of an act at the Dibley talent night is to do an impression of his first cousin (before and after tonsillectomy), and he is routinely described as being a pedantic old fart. Draft Dodging: In "Summer" he mentions having evaded conscription during World War II by hiding in the woods with a strapping farmhand for company. A Fate Worse Than Death: Apparently, listening to his extremely boring stories will eventually be this. He's accused ofboring his own parents to deathand when he substitutes for Geraldine in "Autumn" four members of the congregation actuallydieduring his sermon."That was never proved." Late Coming Out: He is clearly in his sixties when he comes out as gay.

characters.name: Letitia Cropley
characters.description: Cool Old Lady: A good few sandwiches short of a picnic but generally friendly, and every year, she dresses up as the Easter Bunny and delivers chocolate eggs to the village. Cordon Bleugh Chef: Otherwise known as the "The Queen of Cordon Bleurgh", she is theTrope Namer. Shecancook edible food, as she shows during Lent. It's just that, for unfathomable reasons, she decides that putting ketchup on a lovely chocolate cake or liverandchocolate on a sandwich is a good idea. Dirty Old Woman: She has her moments. Forgetful Jones: She has a tendency to forget whatever she has said a moment prior. It especially comes into play in her last request to Geraldine... and everyone else on the Parish Council. I Was Quite a Looker: As a former "corker," she gives this advice to a young woman:"Snog everyone! Sleep with most. I didn't, and I've been regretting it ever since!"
